title: Pseudocode
definition: Pseudocode is a language-independent notation for expressing algorithmic control and data operations precisely enough to inspect and trace.
purpose: Describe an algorithm for human review without binding its meaning to one programming language.
history: Algorithm education and technical publications use many pseudocode conventions; there is no single universal syntax.
mental_model: Pseudocode is a precise bridge between a problem contract and a future implementation.
analogy: An architectural plan guides construction without being the building; the analogy stops because pseudocode must still define executable control precisely.
industry_notes: Teams use prose, pseudocode, diagrams, and executable prototypes at different precision levels; the chosen representation must remain reviewable.
ai_notes: AI-generated pseudocode is an untrusted proposal that must be checked against the problem contract and concrete traces.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to turn a bounded requirement into precise pseudocode and explain notation choices.
exercise_candidates: Remove language-specific syntax from an algorithm while preserving behavior
lab_candidates: Design fare-calculation pseudocode from a problem contract
project_candidates: Specify the Instruction Simulator before implementation
